issues.description: The problem statement's UML specifies numberOfInscribedStudents as an int, but the solution implementation declares numberOfInscribedStudents as a long (and the constructor/getter/setter use long). This type mismatch is structural: students following the UML will implement an int, while the reference solution uses long, which also leads to an inconsistent arithmetic usage in getTotalNumberOfStudents (adding a long and int while the method returns int). This creates potential compile/runtime issues and confusion about the intended type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the types consistent. Either (A) change numberOfInscribedStudents in the solution to int and update the constructor/getter/setter to use int (so all attributes and getTotalNumberOfStudents remain int as in the UML), or (B) update the UML/problem statement to declare numberOfInscribedStudents as long and change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long (and adjust related documentation). Option A is recommended to match the current UML and exercise wording.
